voyage.name: Escapada Cycling
voyage.content: Gravel, e-bike, trekking and mountain bike rental, as well as guided cycling experiences.

voyage.name: Alcazaba
voyage.content: A Moorish castle built in the 11th century on a hill in the middle of the city, this old fort is the best-preserved of its kind in Spain. Upon entering you'll climb up past the ramparts offering excellent views of the city and lush gardens to a small Moorish palace at the top which holds a number of artifacts from excavations on the site.

voyage.name: Roman Theater
voyage.content: The beautiful remains of an old Roman theater. You can view them anytime from the overlook in the plaza, but if you want to get up close you can enter the attached building, where you'll be shown a short film and view some artifacts before entering the theater itself, where you can walk past the old stage and sit on the stone steps.

voyage.name: Castillo de Gibralfaro
voyage.price: €3.50; reduced €1.50, free Sundays after 14:00. Combined ticket with Alcazaba €5.50
voyage.content: Another Moorish castle and the counterpart to the Alcazaba, the Castillo sits on a larger hill behind the Alcazaba and offers an incredible view of the city and neighboring suburbs from the ramparts that encircle the castillo. Within the fortress is a set of gardens and some displays, including an exhibit on the various military forces to have occupied the fort. Between the Castillo and the Alcazaba, visit the Alcaza

voyage.name: Málaga Cathedral
voyage.content: In the heart of the city centre and well worth visiting.

voyage.name: Picasso Museum
voyage.hours: Jul-Aug: daily 10:00-20:00; Mar-Jun Sep-Oct: daily 10:00-19:00; Nov-Dec: daily 10:00-18:00
voyage.address: Palacio de Buenavista, C/ San Agustín 8
voyage.content: The Picasso museum hosts exclusive paintings and other artworks by the Málaga-born artist. Your entry fee also provides access to regularly changing exhibitions by other artists.

voyage.name: Picasso's birthplace
voyage.content: Loads of objects and some paintings that the most famous artist of the 20th century created during his childhood.

voyage.name: Museo Carmen Thyssen
voyage.hours: Tue-Thu 10:00-20:00, Fri Sat 10:00-21:00, Sun and holidays 10:00-20:00 (open Mon and closed Sun in summer)
voyage.content: Opened in 2011 and has an excellent collection of 19th and 20th century Spanish paintings.

voyage.name: Centre Pompidou Málaga
voyage.address: Pasaje Doctor Carrillo Casaux, s/n 29016, Muelle Uno, Puerto de Málaga
voyage.content: Works from the Paris Centre Pompidou's collection.

voyage.name: Museum Jorge Rando
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 10:00-14:00 & 16:00-20:00 Sat 10:00-14:00 (Afternoon session is one hour later June-September)
voyage.content: Museum focussed on expressionist art.

voyage.name: Interactive Museum of Music
voyage.alt: Museo Interactivo de la Musica Málaga
voyage.content: Has one of the largest collections of musical instruments in Europe.

voyage.name: Málaga Glass & Crystal Museum
voyage.alt: Museo del Vidrio y Crystal de Málaga
voyage.address: P. Santísimo Cristo de la Sangre 2,
voyage.content: The museum has around 700 pieces of glass, dating from Phoenician times to the 20th century. Housed in a housed in an 18th-century casa palacio which is as fascinating as the objects within. Guided tours only, available in English, but no additional charge and no appointment needed.

voyage.name: MUCAC - La Coracha
voyage.content: Contemporary art museum that will be open on two sites.

voyage.name: MUCAC - Mayoristas
voyage.content: Former Centro de Arte Contemporáneo will reopen after refurbishment.

voyage.name: Automobile & Fashion Museum
voyage.alt: Museo del Automovil y la Moda
voyage.price: Adult €10; 65+ €8; other concessions & groups €6. (occasional dramatised openings at higher price, check website)
voyage.content: An interest combined museum showing vehicles & fashion through various eras. Located in a former tobacco factory.

voyage.name: Russian Museum Collection, St. Petersburg-Málaga
voyage.address: Avenida Sor Teresa Prat, nº 15, Edificio de Tabacalera
voyage.content: It was the first European subsidiary of the Russian State Museum of Saint Petersburg. However, the museum's collection returned to Russia in May 2022 after concluding the last exhibition. Since then, the Malaga City Council has kept the museum open with exhibitions deposited by private collectors.

voyage.name: Plaza de Toros de la Malagueta
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 10:00-13:00 and 17:00-20:00, closed Sat Sun and holidays
voyage.content: Málaga's bullring.

voyage.name: La Conception Botanical & Historical Garden
voyage.hours: Apr-Sep: Tue-Sun 09:30-20:30; Oct-Mar: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:30; closed Dec 25, Jan 1
voyage.content: Botanical and historical garden with beautiful views of the city from this garden; worth a visit.

voyage.name: Malaga Aviation Museum
voyage.address: Plaza Pierre-Georges Latécoère s/n, 29004 Málaga, Spain
voyage.content: Unique museum with original 1940s terminal in Malaga, other buildings with old and new aviation equipment, uniforms, and models of the airport. Interesting for both children and adults. Free parking.

voyage.name: La Térmica
voyage.content: Former charity house of mercy. Now a cultural centre that hosts occasional exhibitions & small concerts.

voyage.name: Sightseeing Treasure Hunt Málaga
voyage.hours: By appointment, tours last at least 2.5 hours
voyage.content: Malaga City Adventure is a startup company and pioneers in Treasure Hunting Events in Málaga. They offer a Sightseeing Treasure Hunt for tourists and tailor made team building events for companies. Equipped with a treasure hunting bag, a treasure book with information and recommendations and a modern GPS-compass you explore the historical centre of Málaga, search for hidden items and solve challenging riddles to find

voyage.name: La Cochera Caberet
voyage.address: Bus 3 to Camino del Pato or metro
voyage.content: Small music & theatre venue a couple of km out of the centre.

voyage.name: La Trinchera
voyage.content: Concert Hall 2 km west of city centre.

voyage.name: Semana Santa
voyage.content: The Holy Week processions in Málaga are known for at least 500 years, and are one of the oldest in all of Spain. They begin Palm Sunday and end Easter Sunday. The Spanish Legion's procession is a must see on Maundy Thursday.

voyage.name: Central Market
voyage.content: A lively market featuring regional produce and olive oil, fish, meat, and cheese, housed in a 19th-century wrought iron building. Don't miss the restored, enormous stained glass windows, as well as the large 14th-century Moorish gate incorporated into the building's southern façade.

voyage.name: Bodeguita El Gallo
voyage.content: Typical Andalusian tavern evironment, Sweet Málaga wines and the most traditional tapas.

voyage.name: Vegetariano El Calafate
voyage.content: A hidden gem around the corner from Thyssen Museum. Offers traditional Spanish & Andalucian dishes, with a vegetarian twist. Low-key interior with art for sale on the walls. Good choice for lunch and dinner.

voyage.name: Taberna Quitapenas Sánchez Pastor
voyage.content: Good place to go for tapas, nice atmosphere, good service. Authentic and friendly. Great wines.

voyage.name: Taperia El Beato
voyage.content: Great terrace and fantastic service. Fresh fish, homemade croquettes, meatballs in delicious almond sauce.

voyage.name: La Campana
voyage.content: Cozy and typical Andalusian place of Malaga with a lot of history. Cozy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Curry-Ya! Málaga
voyage.content: A very cozy establishment. As the name suggests, a wide variety of curry dishes. Ideal to spend some time with your close ones between spicy and sweet dishes with a Japanese essence. Good service and very good atmosphere.

voyage.name: Tasca La Salita
voyage.content: Yummy tapas (especially the pork) at a good price. Not a touristy place with tons of seats so get there early.

voyage.name: Spago's
voyage.content: Reviews used to be good for this place but was more like lukewarm microwave pasta out 2 minutes after ordering. Try at your own risk.

voyage.name: La Vegana
voyage.content: 100% vegan tapas bar. Saturday is Paella day. See website for hours & reservations.

voyage.name: Noviembre - the flavor house
voyage.content: Healthy food in an attractive open plan street corner restaurant. Gluten-free, Vegetarian & Vegan options

voyage.name: Taberna La Antigua
voyage.content: Typical Spanish tavern. The owner is truly attentive to the needs of customers. Good paella.

voyage.name: Bodega-Bar El Pimpi
voyage.content: Enormously popular with locals and tourists, this place serves up excellent food and wine. Despite being frequented by such celebrities as Antonio Banderas and Placido Domingo, the prices are very moderate.

voyage.name: Mesón Lo Güeno
voyage.content: Offers a large range of tapas and excellent wines.

voyage.name: Restaurante Gallego Candamil
voyage.content: This Galician restaurant is very popular with the locals. This is understandable when you see the great range of quality tapas at fantastic prices, e.g. tapa of empanada €1.25, glass of cider €1.15.

voyage.name: Restaurante @ Parador de Málaga Gibralfaro
voyage.content: Castillo de Gibralfaro. Some report being disappointed by the restaurant at the Parador. The food was sub par, but the service by contrast was exemplary, together with all the nice little free appetizers, aperitifs, etc. Wine list tended towards the expensive but with the excellent idea of a monthly wine choice 'balancing quality and value', for example a very palatable Ribera del Duero Crianza at €10. Set menu €27 p

voyage.name: Jacinto Restaurante
voyage.address: Av. del Obispo Angel Herrera Oria, 7
voyage.content: High-end seafood restaurant

voyage.name: Central Beers
voyage.content: Good choice of Belgian beers. Busy at weekends.

voyage.name: Birras Deluxe
voyage.content: Belgian & American-style beers on tap with friendly staff. Food available.

voyage.name: Tako bar
voyage.content: Mainly Belgian beers with range of Tex-Mex food available.

voyage.name: Oasis Backpackers' Hostel Malaga
voyage.content: It has a big roof-top terrace to overlook Málaga and a bar in the basement. Free Wi-Fi and breakfast. From €14, dorms and double rooms. Directions: From Bus station Paseo los Tilos it's a 2-km walk to the Oasis Hostel at Calle San Telmo 14. Walk to the right of Paseo los Tilos turning into Callejones del Perchel. At the roundabout take a right into Avenida de la Aurora crossing the river. Continue on the river bank o

voyage.name: Pension La Palma
voyage.content: Run by a friendly lady, this cheap and cheerful place has rooms starting from €30. It's very central and some rooms have little balconies.

voyage.name: Pension Costa Rica
voyage.content: Very primitive and in the middle of the red light district, but it seems to be one of the cheapest available.

voyage.name: Picasso's Corner
voyage.content: Right in the historic district, close to the beach. Bar and lounge, food and disco shows.

voyage.name: Hotel Alameda
voyage.address: Street Casas de campos, 3 (corner street Cordoba,9)
voyage.content: Economic budget between the historical centre and the port. All rooms have private bathrooms, television and air-conditioning or heating. The hotel is on the eighth floor of a building shared with other businesses and you will need to use the buzzer (well labelled) to speak to reception so they can let you in. (Reception is staffed 24 hours a day.)

voyage.name: Apartamentos Debambú
voyage.content: Centrally located, with very clean rooms. Exceptionally clean and modern, with helpful staff. Free wi-fi, airport shuttle available.

voyage.name: Málaga Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel with garden, swimming pool, jacuzzi, restaurant. Boardwalk with beach restaurants (chiringuitos).

voyage.name: Oficentro Suites
voyage.content: The apartment is fully furnished and cleaning is done weekly.

voyage.name: Silken Puerta Málaga
voyage.content: Very stylish four-star from the Silken chain, opposite the main train station. Beautifully decorated rooms and bathrooms, with great attention to detail. Good discounted rates in winter (€56-69+VAT).

voyage.name: Suites del Pintor
voyage.content: Bright, comfortable apartments in Malaga's historic centre

voyage.name: Hotel MS Maestranza Málaga
voyage.content: Nice 4-star hotel in the centre of Malaga.

voyage.name: Higueron Hotel Malaga, Curio Collection by Hilton
ibis budget Málaga Centro
voyage.content: Well located comfortable basic budget hotel from French Hotel chain with good wifi.

voyage.name: NH Málaga
voyage.content: In the historic and commercial centre of Málaga, next to the 'Puente de la Esperanza' and a short stroll from the 'Museo de la Expiración'. Its excellent location makes it easy to enjoy Málaga's unique personality.

voyage.name: Parador de Málaga Gibralfaro
voyage.content: Fantastic location with spectacular views (best on 3rd floor) over the city. Sitting area and balcony.

voyage.name: Hotel del Pintor
voyage.content: Opened in 2005, the Hotel del Pintor is a small urban hotel that combines design and technology with personalized attention. Central location in the historic centre, near Picasso's birthplace. €74-121.
